title: Gold Miners or Silver Miners: Which Precious Metals ETF Is the Better Buy Right Now?
author: Sara Appino
description: The article compares two precious metals mining ETFs: Sprott Gold Miners ETF (SGDM), which focuses on North American gold producers with a lower 0.46% expense ratio, and Global X Silver Miners ETF (SIL), which provides global silver exposure with higher 1-year returns (83% vs 53%) but greater volatility. Gold miners are recommended for new precious metals investors, while silver miners suit those seeking higher-conviction bets on industrial and monetary demand convergence.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Lower expense ratio (0.46%), more stable with lower beta (0.53) and maximum drawdown (45%), better 5-year growth ($2,214 from $1,000), and recommended as the more established entry point for new precious metals investors.

Higher 1-year returns (83%), higher dividend yield (1.10%), and positioned as a higher-conviction bet for investors with existing precious metals exposure seeking exposure to industrial demand and green transition themes.

title: SIL vs. GDX: Silver Miners Outpaced Gold Miners in 2025. Will It Last?
author: Sara Appino
description: Silver miners ETF (SIL) delivered 135.40% returns over 12 months, significantly outpacing gold miners ETF (GDX) at 91.10%. While SIL offers higher returns and dividend yield, GDX provides lower costs, larger assets, and greater diversification. Both funds carry higher volatility than physical metals, with SIL experiencing steeper drawdowns historically. The choice depends on investor risk tolerance and market outlook.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Delivered exceptional 135.40% 1-year returns, higher dividend yield (1.10%), and outperformed gold miners significantly. However, higher expense ratio (0.65%) and greater volatility (max drawdown -55.60%) present risks.

Offers lower expense ratio (0.51%), larger asset base ($31.3B), better diversification (54 holdings), and lower volatility (max drawdown -46.50%). Solid 91.10% 1-year returns with more stability make it suitable for conservative investors.

title: Metals ETF Investing: GLD Offers Stability While SIL Brings Higher Risk and Reward
author: Sarah Sidlow
description: GLD and SIL offer different approaches to precious metals investing. GLD provides direct exposure to physical gold with lower costs and greater stability, while SIL invests in silver mining companies with higher volatility but stronger recent returns (140% vs 49.92% over one year). The choice depends on investor risk tolerance and investment goals.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: SIL shows strong recent performance (140% 1-yr return vs GLD's 49.92%) and is positioned as attractive for risk-tolerant investors bullish on silver and its industrial applications. However, noted for higher volatility and deeper drawdowns (-56.79% max drawdown).

title: Why Are Coeur Mining Shares Trading Higher On Wednesday?
author: Lekha Gupta
description: Coeur Mining shares rose 6.37% in premarket trading on Wednesday following the company's announcement of a private exchange offer for $40 million in senior notes and positive 2026 guidance. Post-acquisition of New Gold Inc., the company expects gold production of 680,000-815,000 ounces and approved a $750 million share repurchase program and new dividend. The stock carries a Buy rating with a $14.59 average price target.

title: Gold, Silver Crash Sparks Mining Meltdown: 10 Stocks Crater On Fed Warsh Shock
author: Piero Cingari
description: Gold and silver prices collapsed on Friday, with silver down 27% and gold down 9.5% — their worst single-day declines since 1980. The selloff was triggered by President Trump's nomination of Kevin Warsh as Federal Reserve chair, perceived as a hawk who prioritizes inflation control over monetary stimulus. This unwound the 'debasement trade' that had driven precious metals higher in January, causing mining stocks to suffer double-digit losses.
